mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1.5% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during similar rate-unchanged periods (p > 0.05), or the FEDFUNDS rate does not remain elevated for the required duration.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening labor market, which anticipates higher corporate profits and boosts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same or
failure_condition: The correlation between PAYEMS growth and UNRATE decline is not statistically significant (p > 0.05), or 20-day forward returns are not higher than in comparable labor expansion periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% for three consecutive months suggests accelerating economic demand, which elevates expectations of future corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO month-over-month growth > 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: INDPRO growth does not sustain the required magnitude for the specified horizon, or 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months suggests the Fed may maintain current policy, reducing policy uncertainty and allowing equity valuation multiples to expand, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL does not exhibit the required decline, or 20-day forward returns are not higher than during comparable low-inflation periods.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the GDP deflator (not in the catalog, so use GDPC1 as proxy for inflation) turns positive while the Federal Funds rate remains steady, it indicates a shift from deflationary to inflationary expectations, which can compress equity forward discount rates and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 month-over-month change turns positive while FEDFUNDS remains constant for two months
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not statistically lower than during deflationary transitions with similar FEDFUNDS behavior (p > 0.05), or the inflation signal is not clearly detected.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in job openings (PAYEMS) accompanied by a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests a cooling labor market, which can erode consumer and business confidence and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by at least 5% in a month while UNRATE increases by at least 0.3 percentage points
failure_condition: The relationship between falling job openings and rising unemployment is not statistically significant (p > 0.05), or 5-day forward returns are not statistically lower than in comparable labor market cooling episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining consumer sentiment (not directly observable, so proxy with HOUST industrial production or a supply-side proxy) coupled with sustained low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2%) suggests supply-side easing that can support higher equity valuations and positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines for three consecutive months while CPIAUCSL remains below 2%
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than during comparable supply-side easing episodes (p > 0.05), or the supply indicators do not align as hypothesized.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of unexpectedly high inflation (indicated by a sharp increase in CPIAUCSL) while the Fed maintains a steady FEDFUNDS rate, investors anticipate future rate hikes, which increases discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by at least 1% month-over-month for two consecutive months while FEDFUNDS remains unchanged
regime_hint: unexpectedly high inflation with steady rates
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically lower than during similar inflation surprises with unchanged rates (p > 0.05), or the inflation signal is not clearly detected.
